## Resolved

### F-790 — A test group's import crashed the deployed viewer pod

> _2026-11-21 · realm/blong-viewer · resolved_

A release pod for the viewer crash-looped on `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @feasibleone/lukaot`, imported
from `realm/blong-viewer/server/test/test/testViewerFlow.ts`, although the group is test-only and
the pod runs `release`. The cause is the loader's layer discovery: it imports every well-known
folder's module to read the activation beside it, so `server/test/` is _evaluated_ in every process
— and the group's module imports whatever its tests need. `@feasibleone/lukaot` was a devDependency,
so the artifact did not carry it and the import failed at load, before any activation was consulted.

The rule that follows: a realm's source must resolve in the artifact, and a test group is still
source. A package a test group imports at module level belongs in `dependencies` — the deploy
closure is what makes the file loadable, and `devDependencies` are excluded from it.

The other half is the artifact's own check: a deploy cycle is the only thing that evaluates this
path, because a dev run resolves lukaot from the repository. `kubectl logs` on the crash-looping pod
named the file and the package in one line, which is what made it a two-minute diagnosis once the
pod was read.

Verified: realm/blong-viewer declares @feasibleone/lukaot in dependencies (no devDependency copy),
so the test group resolves in a release artifact; F-791 is the same incident recorded from the
loader's side, and the fix is the dependency move the code carries.

### F-793 — A realm served by its own Service had no Ingress path

> _2026-11-21 · realm/blong-viewer · resolved_

The deployed viewer answered viewer.entry.find only from inside its own pod; every browser call
failed with JOSE Header missing. The live Ingress for the portal listed the realm paths and a
catch-all /rpc/ and no /rpc/viewer, so a sealed body went to the portal process, which has no viewer
route and refused it as an encrypted body on a route that does not require auth. The generator built
the ingress from the portal deployments and stopped there: a realm whose namespace is answered by a
Service of its own, with no deployment listing that namespace, had no path. The rule is now that
every Service of the plan is routed, and the first attempt was wrong in a way worth naming: it
skipped a Service whose name a Deployment carries, to avoid a route nothing calls, and the viewer's
Service and its Deployment share one name — so the skip removed exactly the realm the rule exists
for. A hand patch made it look fixed until the next pass regenerated the tree and dropped the path.

Done and verified on the deployment: the ingress carries /rpc/viewer -> viewer, generated from the
tree rather than patched, and the page loads entries with the stream open. A regression step
(aServiceNamedAfterItsProcessIsStillRouted) asserts the path.

### F-794 — A contributed page drew its own grid in the portal palette

> _2026-11-21 · realm/blong-viewer · resolved_

The portal page for the viewer rendered the light grid inside a dark portal. The viewer draws its
own grid and its own colours through svar-ui, so it cannot inherit a palette from CSS the portal
sets; the palette has to be handed to it. The portal already exposes useThemePalette for exactly
this and blong-browser's own MermaidRenderer reads it, so a page that draws its own surface is
expected to read the hook and pass the mode down, not to hope a theme context reaches it.

Done: logViewerPage.tsx reads useThemePalette and passes theme={{mode}}, and the deployed page draws
the dark grid inside the dark portal.
